hypotheses.reasoning: The origin is the external card processor (api.cardproc.example). Healthy payment-svc /charge calls completed in roughly 20-90ms all through the window until 18:04:54, when the first 'card processor call slow: 3576ms' warning appeared (#727). Latency then escalated to 11636ms (#757) and then to hard 30s timeouts (#845 at 18:07:14, #929 at 18:08:43). The calls are hanging rather than failing fast, which points to a dependency timeout. payment-svc is the direct point of failure. order-service then saw ReadTimeout (#930), its connection pool to payment-svc saturated at 50/50 with requests queued (#931), and checkout pool checkout timeouts followed (#995). Those are downstream amplification, so I did not cite them. The api-gateway 503s (#906, #1019, #1128, #1189) are the customer-visible symptom. Ruled out: postgres (checkpoints and vacuums are routine, no lock or slowness), redis (0 errors, normal hit rate), and metrics-agent (its queue drops are a side effect of load/noise, not the cause of checkout failures). No deploy lines were found. Not fully certain between dependency_timeout and external_outage, because the processor's own status is not visible in our logs; the hanging-call pattern favours dependency_timeout.

The card processor could be down or degraded on its side, since it is a third party with no logs of its own here. The same lines would fit an outage, but the gradual latency climb before the hard failures suggests a hang rather than an outright outage.

verdict.recommendedAction: Treat the card processor (api.cardproc.example) as the faulty dependency. Engage the payment provider and check their status and incident channel. In the meantime, reduce the impact on checkout: lower the payment-svc timeout to the card processor (30s is too long and is holding order-service connections), add a circuit breaker to fail fast when the processor is slow, and consider raising or queueing the order-service-to-payment-svc connection pool limit (currently 50). Once the processor recovers, confirm that the pool drains and /checkout returns to 200s.

hypotheses.reasoning: The origin is the external card processor (api.cardproc.example). Healthy payment-svc /charge calls completed in roughly 20-90ms all through the window until 18:04:54, when the first 'card processor call slow: 3576ms' warning appeared (#727). Latency then escalated to 11636ms (#757) and then to hard 30s timeouts (#845 at 18:07:14, #929 at 18:08:43). The calls are hanging rather than failing fast, which points to a dependency timeout. payment-svc is the direct point of failure. order-service then saw ReadTimeout (#930), its connection pool to payment-svc saturated at 50/50 with requests queued (#931), and checkout pool checkout timeouts followed (#995). Those are downstream amplification, so I did not cite them. The api-gateway 503s (#906, #1019, #1128, #1189) are the customer-visible symptom. Ruled out: postgres (checkpoints and vacuums are routine, no lock or slowness), redis (0 errors, normal hit rate), and metrics-agent (its queue drops are a side effect of load/noise, not the cause of checkout failures). No deploy lines were found. Not fully certain between dependency_timeout and external_outage, because the processor's own status is not visible in our logs; the hanging-call pattern favours dependency_timeout.

The card processor could be down or degraded on its side, since it is a third party with no logs of its own here. The same lines would fit an outage, but the gradual latency climb before the hard failures suggests a hang rather than an outright outage.

input.recommendedAction: Treat the card processor (api.cardproc.example) as the faulty dependency. Engage the payment provider and check their status and incident channel. In the meantime, reduce the impact on checkout: lower the payment-svc timeout to the card processor (30s is too long and is holding order-service connections), add a circuit breaker to fail fast when the processor is slow, and consider raising or queueing the order-service-to-payment-svc connection pool limit (currently 50). Once the processor recovers, confirm that the pool drains and /checkout returns to 200s.
